accepted.question_text: Let X be a topological space. Let O be the family of open covers of X, let Gamma be the family of open gamma-covers (infinite open covers where each x in X belongs to all but finitely many members), and let Omega be the family of open omega-covers (for each finite F subset of X, some cover element contains F). Using Ufin(A,B): for each sequence of covers from A with no finite subcover, choose finite subfamilies so that the sequence of unions is in B; and Sfin(A,B): for each sequence of covers from A, choose finite subfamilies whose union is in B. Is Ufin(O,Omega) equal to Sfin(Gamma,Omega)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 ([30]). (1) Is Ufin(O, Ω) = Sfin(Γ, Ω)?

accepted.question_text: With the same definitions of Ufin and Sfin for cover classes, if Ufin(O,Omega) is not equal to Sfin(Gamma,Omega), does Ufin(O,Gamma) imply Sfin(Gamma,Omega)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 ([30]). (2) And if not, does Ufin(O, Γ) imply Sfin(Γ, Ω)?

accepted.question_text: Can a Borel non-sigma-compact subgroup of a Polish group be generated by a subspace that satisfies Ufin(O,Gamma) (the Hurewicz-type selection property described in the paper)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2 ([81]). Can a Borel non-σ-compact subgroup of a Polish group be generated by a subspace satisfying Ufin(O, Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Assume X subseteq B subseteq R, B is Borel, and X satisfies Ufin(O,Gamma). Must there exist a sigma-compact set F with X subset F subset B? Also, if the Borel assumption on B is strengthened to B being F_{sigma delta}, is the conclusion true?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3 ([6, preprint version]). Assume that X ⊆ B ⊆ R, B is Borel, and X satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Must there be a σ-compact F with X ⊂ F ⊂ B? What if B is Fσδ?
Update 1. “No”, and b = d suffices for that [6, final version].

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a set of reals X satisfying S1(Gamma,Gamma) whose cardinality is b?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 ([12]). Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals X satisfying S1(Γ, Γ) such that |X| = b?
Update 2. “No”, and the counter-example is Laver’s model [38].

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a set of reals satisfying Sfin(Omega,Omega) of cardinality d?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 ([74]). Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals satisfying Sfin(Ω, Ω) such that |X| = d?

accepted.question_text: Is there a direct (non-dichotomic) construction of a set of reals M satisfying Sfin(Omega,Omega) but not Ufin(O,Gamma)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3 ([74]). Is there a direct (non-dichotomic) construction of a set of reals M satisfying Sfin(Ω, Ω) but not Ufin(O, Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Is Borel's Conjecture for Sfin(B,B) consistent, where B is the class of countable Borel covers?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4 ([45]). Is Borel’s Conjecture for Sfin(B,B) consistent?

accepted.question_text: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply realizations of the consistent settings (d), (e), (g), (j), and (l) in the Borel Scheepers-diagram classification presented in Figure 4?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply a realization of the settings (d),(e),(g),(j), and (l)?

accepted.question_text: Does Martin's Axiom imply the existence of a set of reals of cardinality continuum satisfying S1(BOmega,BGamma)?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 ([42]). Does Martin’s Axiom imply the existence of a set of reals of cardinality continuum, satisfying S1(BΩ,BΓ)?

accepted.question_text: For X, let L(F) be closure of a family F of subsets of X under lim inf, and say X has the delta-property if for each open omega-cover U of X, X is in L(U). Is this delta-property equivalent to the property Omega choose Gamma (equivalently S1(Omega,Gamma))?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 ([22]). Is the δ-property equivalent to Ω Γ ?
Update 4. “Yes” in the Borel case [44].

accepted.question_text: If (X_n) is an increasing sequence of sets of reals each satisfying Omega choose Gamma (that is, S1(Omega,Gamma)), must the union also satisfy Omega choose Gamma?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2 ([42]). Does every union of an increasing sequence {Xn}n∈N of sets satisfying Ω Γ satisfy Ω Γ ?
Update 5. “Yes” [29].

accepted.question_text: Are either of the Borel selection classes S1(BOmega,BOmega) or Sfin(BOmega,BOmega) preserved by finite powers?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3 ([57]). Are any of the classes S1(BΩ,BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ,BΩ) preserved by finite powers?

accepted.question_text: Is the class S1(BOmega,BGamma) preserved by finite powers?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4 ([57]). Is S1(BΩ,BΓ) preserved by finite powers?

accepted.question_text: Is the class Ufin(O,Gamma) intersect S1(O,O) preserved by finite products?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.6. Is Ufin(O, Γ) ∩ S1(O, O) preserved by finite products?

accepted.question_text: Is Sfin(Omega,Omega) consistently additive (that is, can there be a model where finite or countable unions preserve this property as required by additivity)?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.10 ([70]). Is Sfin(Ω, Ω) consistently additive?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist, in ZFC, topological groups G and H such that each satisfies Sfin(Onbd,O) but the product G x H fails Sfin(Onbd,O)?
